status: Commerce now has a bounded native quotation/sales-order document read and safe owner-local lifecycle slice: quote submit, independent approve, return-to-draft, draft cancel, independent confirmed-quote cancel and quote conversion to a draft sales order; sales draft submit/return/cancel; Company/branch-scoped document read with current IAM, versions/CAS, idempotency, audit/outbox, rollback and persisted readback. Sales-order approval and confirmed sales-order cancellation remain retained because their Finance credit and Inventory reversal guards are not exposed as native public ports; they fail closed in the native layer instead of bypassing those guards. Purchase, fulfillment, invoicing, returns and the remaining Commerce workflows remain retained.

scope.workflowBoundary: The qualified slice is the order detail read and the owner-local state transitions that do not move stock or post Finance: quote submit/approve/return/cancel(draft or independently confirmed)/convert, and sales submit/return/cancel(draft). Purchase orders, order create/update, sales approval, confirmed sales-order cancellation, reservation changes, fulfillment, invoicing, settlement, returns, customer notifications, posting setup and every other Commerce workflow remain retained TypeScript.
scope.domain: Current actor policy (selected-context expiry, sales module, commerce.read/commerce.sales/commerce.approve), exact Company and optional branch/department scope, quote/sales kind restriction, bounded date/currency/text/amount validation, unique ordered lines, document totals equal line totals, stock lines require a warehouse, exact transition matrix, independent quote approver/canceller, discount-approval reason, conversion identity, exact receipt `{id,state,version,salesId}` and persisted readback projections. Sales approval returns COMMERCE_SALES_APPROVAL_FINANCE_GUARD and confirmed sales cancellation returns ORDER_REVERSAL_REQUIRED; neither path weakens the retained cross-owner guard.
scope.application: order_detail re-checks the current IAM assignment before the scoped owner read. transition_order authorizes write and current IAM, validates and trims the exact command, serializes the command key with a transaction-scoped advisory lock, resolves the idempotency receipt before the scoped locked order, applies one exact expected-version CAS, writes receipt/audit/outbox in the same unit, converts a confirmed quote into one draft sales order plus copied lines, and validates persisted order/sales readback before returning.
scope.adapters: SQL is Commerce-owned (`commerce_orders`, `commerce_order_lines`, `commerce_products`, `commerce_fulfillments`) plus shared `command_receipts`, `audit_events` and `outbox_events`. Current IAM is re-read through existing assignments/iam_role_allows/iam_assignment_active/iam_principal_active predicates. No Inventory, Finance, Quality, Sales or Files row is read or mutated by this slice. The caller's serializable Holding transaction is required; no transaction is opened, committed or retried here.
scope.http: Owner-local GET /api/v1/holdings/{holding_slug}/commerce/orders/{order_id} and POST /api/v1/holdings/{holding_slug}/commerce/orders/{order_id}/transition. Exact registered Host/Holding targets and HTTPS origins, strict Idempotency-Key/Content-Type/JSON body validation, bounded bodies, unknown query rejection, private/no-store plus no-referrer/nosniff responses, and bounded BusinessError status mapping. The composition backend receives transport facts only and must supply the normal Account session, selected Company/branch/department scope, feature/package admission and serializable owner unit.
scope.transport: ERPX_NATIVE_COMMERCE_ORDER_CONFIG is strictly validated: loopback-only private base, reserved ports 3000/3001/3100/3101/3103/8080 plus 5432/5433/5435 and 3200-3299 excluded, exact HTTPS Holding origins, unique hosts/slugs, 250..30000 ms timeout, bounded cookie/context/workspace headers, exact document/receipt shapes, Company/scope coherence, unique ordered lines, line totals equal order totals and a 2 MiB response bound. A configured failure never falls back to the retained reader or command.
scope.ssr: The Commerce order detail page uses native quote/sales order and line rows when ERPX_NATIVE_COMMERCE_ORDER_CONFIG is present, merging retained cross-owner display labels (`party_name`, `warehouse_name`) from getOrder. An unset configuration retains getOrder for the document. Once configured, an invalid or failed native read is surfaced through the existing page error policy rather than silently replaced. Purchase orders and all non-order sections remain retained.
scope.commandRoute: The workplace POST /commerce/orders/{id}/transition route dispatches to native only after a Commerce-owned orderFacts preflight selects a quote (all supported actions) or a sales order (submit/return, and cancel only while draft). Sales approval, confirmed sales cancellation, sales conversion and purchase remain retained by design. Once an order/action is native-eligible, a native or preflight failure is surfaced and never replaced by transitionOrder.
scope.crossOwnerGuards: This slice introduces no Inventory, Finance or Quality effect, so no such same-transaction guard is bypassed. Sales approval still requires the retained Finance credit-limit guard and confirmed sales cancellation still requires the retained Inventory reservation/reversal guard; both are refused natively rather than reimplemented with cross-owner SQL.
scope.notClaimed: No browser journey, authenticated page render, shared composition mount, catalogue acceptance qualification, purchase/order create-update, sales approval, confirmed sales cancellation, fulfillment, invoicing, settlement, return, notification or job verification.
